newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thailand has finally decided to seek help from the International Monetary Fund to salvage its ailing economy. The Finance Ministry is expected today to seek approval from the council of economic ministers to hold talks with IMF officials for the drafting of a comprehensive fiscal, monetary and economic rehabilitation plan. However, Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya denied that the decision to seek IMF help to draw up the plan meant Thailand had decided to take loans from the IMF. (BANGKOK POST)

- Two Italian tourists who were shot at Chiang Mai's international airport on Saturday by an irate policeman who lost a lover to a Caucausian man are out of danger. Police Corporal Rungroj Somjat was arrested yesterday at a guesthouse in the Mae Rim district and charged with attempted murder. The officer admitted to the charge. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand and Vietnam have reached a landmark agreement to settle their boundary disputes in the Gulf of Thailand, a senior Foreign Ministry official said. THe agreement was expected to be signed shortly, bringing to an end potential conflicts arising from unclear sea boundaries in the gulf. (THE NATION)

- The fate of the 16 beleaguered finance companies is still hanging in the balance although the government has agreed to give them another 104 days for official approval of their rescue plans. (THE NATION)

- Financiers agree that the government must take a more aggressive, open attitude in restructuring the economy. Finance Minister Thanong said last week that within a fortnight he would announce new steps to achieve this. But others say that the action is urgently needed now, and that the government must boost confidence in the economy to stop capital outflow, including considering loans from international financial institutions (BANGKOK POST)
